name: scoop-install
body: Windows users install via a Scoop bucket: `scoop bucket add kalide https://github.com/really-knows-ai/kalide` then `scoop install kalide` (manifest `bucket/kalide.json`); `scoop update kalide` upgrades. The manifest uses Scoop's standard `architecture` block: a `64bit` entry with `url` + `hash` for `kalide-windows-amd64` when windows/amd64 is released, and an `arm64` entry with `url` + `hash` for `kalide-windows-arm64` when windows/arm64 is released; each entry is present when its target is released, so the manifest covers exactly the Windows targets actually released (see supported-platforms). URLs are plain public release-download URLs (`https://github.com/really-knows-ai/kalide/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/kalide-windows-<arch>`, aliased to `kalide.exe` via the `#/kalide.exe` fragment or equivalent), fetched anonymously (global.constraint.anonymous-install). The manifest uses Scoop's standard `url` + `hash` download form with no `pre_install` script and no `KALIDE_GITHUB_TOKEN` reference. `bucket/README.md` documents this tokenless flow. AC: on a clean Windows x64 machine (and on Windows ARM when windows/arm64 is supported) with no GitHub credentials, install succeeds and `kalide` runs; `bucket/kalide.json` uses the standard `url`/`hash` form with no `pre_install` and no `KALIDE_GITHUB_TOKEN` reference; `bucket/README.md` describes a tokenless flow.
